2: //!
3: //! This module implements file-level checks for variables that might not be
4: //! defined before use. It wraps 6 related MATLAB Code Analyzer checks into a
5: //! single rule engine that leverages the symbol table and definite-assignment
6: //! analysis.
7: //!
8: //! ## Checks
9: //!
10: //! | ID | Description |
11: //! |----|-------------|
12: //! | NODEF | Variable might not be defined before use |
13: //! | USENS | Variable used but might not be set in all code paths |
14: //! | PSET | Variable set in one branch but not others |
15: //! | SUSENS | Script variable used before set |
16: //! | SVNODEF | Variable in script might not be defined |
17: //! | STOUT | Output variable might not be assigned |
18: //!
19: //! ## Configuration
20: //!

22: //! [lint.rules.UNSET_VARIABLES_ENGINE]

65: /// File-level rule engine that detects variables that might not be defined
66: /// before use. Emits diagnostics under multiple check IDs depending on context.
67: pub struct UnsetVariablesEngine {
68:     /// Rule-specific configuration (retained for future use / serialization).
69:     _config: UnsetVariablesConfig,
70:     /// Precomputed set of ignored names (builtins + user-configured).
71:     ignore_set: HashSet<String>,

74: impl UnsetVariablesEngine {
75:     /// Factory constructor — reads rule-specific params from config.
76:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
77:         let rule_config: UnsetVariablesConfig = config.rule_params("UNSET_VARIABLES_ENGINE");
78:         let mut ignore_set: HashSet<String> =
79:             MATLAB_BUILTINS.iter().map(|s| (*s).to_string()).collect();
80:         for name in &rule_config.ignore {
81:             ignore_set.insert(name.clone());
82:         }
83:         Box::new(Self {
84:             _config: rule_config,
85:             ignore_set,
86:         })
87:     }

89:     /// Check whether a variable name should be ignored.
90:     fn is_ignored(&self, name: &str) -> bool {

98:     /// Run definite-assignment analysis on function scopes and emit diagnostics.
99:     fn check_function_scopes(
100:         &self,
101:         tree: &Tree,
102:         source: &str,
103:         symbol_table: &SymbolTable,
104:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
105:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();

109:             if !matches!(

111:                 ScopeKind::Function
112:                     | ScopeKind::LocalFunction
113:                     | ScopeKind::NestedFunction
114:                     | ScopeKind::Method
115:             ) {
116:                 continue;
117:             }
118:

120:             let Some(func_node) = find_function_node_at(tree, &scope.byte_range) else {

122:             };
123: 
124:             // Run definite-assignment analysis.
125:             let da = analyze_definite_assignment(func_node, source);
126: 
127:             // Emit NODEF/USENS for possibly-unset variables.
128:             self.emit_possibly_unset_diagnostics(&da, &mut diagnostics);
129: 
130:             // Check output arguments: STOUT.
131:             self.check_output_args(scope, &da, &mut diagnostics);
132:         }

135:     }

137:     /// Emit diagnostics for possibly-unset variables from definite-assignment results.
138:     fn emit_possibly_unset_diagnostics(

142:     ) {
143:         // Track which variable names have already been reported to avoid duplicates.
144:         let mut reported: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
145: 
146:         for unset_var in &da.possibly_unset {
147:             if self.is_ignored(&unset_var.name) {
148:                 continue;
149:             }
150:             if reported.contains(&unset_var.name) {
151:                 continue;
152:             }
153:             reported.insert(unset_var.name.clone());
154: 
155:             // If the variable is in the definitely-assigned set at function end
156:             // but was used before that point, it's USENS (used but not set in
157:             // all paths). Otherwise it's NODEF (never defined at all on some paths).
158:             let (rule_id, message) = if da.definitely_assigned.contains(&unset_var.name) {

528:     /// Find the location of the first assignment to a variable within a compound

530:     fn find_assignment_location(

532:         node: Node,

534:         var_name: &str,
535:     ) -> Option<(std::ops::Range<usize>, usize, usize)> {
536:         // DFS search for the first assignment to var_name.
537:         let mut stack = vec![node];
538:         while let Some(current) = stack.pop() {
539:             if current.kind() == "assignment" {
540:                 if let Some(lhs) = current.child_by_field_name("left") {
541:                     if lhs.kind() == "identifier" {
542:                         let name = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
543:                         if name == var_name {
544:                             let pos = lhs.start_position();
545:                             return Some((
546:                                 lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte(),
547:                                 pos.row + 1,
548:                                 pos.column + 1,
549:                             ));
550:                         }
551:                     }
552:                 }
553:             }
554:             // Push children in reverse so we visit left-to-right.
555:             let count = current.child_count();

622: /// Find a `function_definition` node in the tree that matches the given byte range.
623: ///
624: /// Performs a DFS from the root, returning the first `function_definition` node
625: /// whose byte range matches.
626: fn find_function_node_at<'a>(tree: &'a Tree, byte_range: &std::ops::Range<usize>) -> Option<Node<'a>> {
627:     let mut stack = vec![tree.root_node()];
628:     while let Some(node) = stack.pop() {
629:         if node.kind() == "function_definition"
630:             && node.start_byte() == byte_range.start
631:             && node.end_byte() == byte_range.end
632:         {
633:             return Some(node);
634:         }
635:         // Only recurse into nodes that overlap with the target range.
636:         let count = node.child_count();
637:         for i in (0..count).rev() {
638:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
639:                 if child.start_byte() <= byte_range.end && child.end_byte() >= byte_range.start {
640:                     stack.push(child);
641:                 }
642:             }
643:         }
644:     }
645:     None
646: }
647: 
648: /// Collect all variable names assigned in a block (shallow — only direct
649: /// assignment statements, not nested blocks).
650: fn collect_block_assignments(block: Node, source: &str) -> HashSet<String> {
651:     let mut assigned = HashSet::new();
652:     let count = block.child_count();
653:     for i in 0..count {
654:         let Some(child) = block.child(i) else {
655:             continue;
656:         };
657:         if child.kind() == "assignment" {
658:             if let Some(lhs) = child.child_by_field_name("left") {
659:                 match lhs.kind() {
660:                     "identifier" => {
661:                         let name = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
662:                         assigned.insert(name.to_string());
663:                     }
664:                     "multioutput_variable" => {
665:                         let lhs_count = lhs.child_count();
666:                         for j in 0..lhs_count {
667:                             if let Some(id) = lhs.child(j) {
668:                                 if id.kind() == "identifier" {
669:                                     let name = &source[id.start_byte()..id.end_byte()];
670:                                     assigned.insert(name.to_string());
671:                                 }
672:                             }
673:                         }
674:                     }
675:                     _ => {}
676:                 }
677:             }
678:         }
679:     }
680:     assigned
681: }
